core_obligations: Compute the cohomology (proof lines 3442-3470): writing the scheme as the spectrum of a finite separable algebra and choosing a finite Galois extension containing its factors, the tensor product of that algebra with the extension splits as a product of copies of the extension indexed by the embeddings; additivity and base change identify the tensor product of the cohomologies with the product of copies of the cohomology of the spectrum of the extension field; comparing dimensions and using nonvanishing shows that the cohomology of the zero dimensional scheme sits in degree zero only and has dimension equal to the degree of the field extension, that the same holds for the extension field, and that the degree zero part of the original is a separable algebra over the coefficient field.

Identify the degree map with the trace (proof lines 3470-3494): the displayed isomorphism is given by the action of the embeddings, and the degree map of the product over the base, computed with the trace over a disjoint union, expresses the degree of an element as the sum of its images under the induced embeddings; after extending scalars to an algebraic closure these become a full set of embeddings of the degree zero part into the closure, so the degree map is the trace map.

Unit and degree of the fundamental class (proof lines 3494-3502): the cycle class of the scheme is one by the unit lemma, and its degree is the degree of the structure morphism because the trace of one is the degree of the field extension.
proof_roadmap: Split the cohomology using a finite Galois extension and additivity.
Read off the cohomological dimension, the separability and the trace description of the degree map.
Apply the unit lemma for the fundamental class and compute its degree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves six statements about a smooth projective scheme of dimension zero: vanishing of the cohomology in nonzero degrees, separability of the degree zero part, its dimension, the identification of the degree map with the trace, the fundamental class being one, and the degree of the fundamental class (statement lines 3431-3446). The proof (proof lines 3447-3502) performs a Galois splitting of the coefficient algebra, uses additivity and base change to compute the cohomology, and identifies the trace. H3: a multi part computation with a Galois descent step, written out in full.
